title: Counterfactual Trajectories with geom_kodom_branch
text: dataset simulates 8 patients diabetes trial. patient pre-randomisation HbA1c readings (observed, medication = NA), continued post-randomisation observed path, model-predicted trajectories two drug arms ("DrugA" "DrugB"). Branch (randomisation) timing differs across patients.
code: set.seed(21)  n_patients <- 8L branch_times <- c(4, 6, 4, 8, 6, 4, 6, 8) # month of randomisation horizon <- 18L # last prediction month  make_patient <- function(i) {   t_branch <- branch_times[i]   base <- rnorm(1, mean = 8.0, sd = 0.8)    # Pre-branch observed visits (every 2 months, including month 0)   t_pre <- seq(0, t_branch, by = 2)   v_pre <- base + cumsum(c(0, rnorm(length(t_pre) - 1L, -0.1, 0.25)))    # Post-branch observed (patient actually received DrugA)   t_post <- seq(t_branch + 2, horizon, by = 2)   v_post <- tail(v_pre, 1L) + cumsum(rnorm(length(t_post), -0.18, 0.2))    # Predictions under DrugA (steeper decline)   v_a <- tail(v_pre, 1L) + cumsum(rep(-0.20, length(t_post))) +     rnorm(length(t_post), 0, 0.1)    # Predictions under DrugB (milder decline)   v_b <- tail(v_pre, 1L) + cumsum(rep(-0.10, length(t_post))) +     rnorm(length(t_post), 0, 0.1)    rbind(     data.frame(       subject_id = sprintf("P%02d", i),       month = t_pre,       hba1c = pmax(5, v_pre),       medication = NA_character_,       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     data.frame(       subject_id = sprintf("P%02d", i),       month = t_post,       hba1c = pmax(5, v_post),       medication = NA_character_,       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     data.frame(       subject_id = sprintf("P%02d", i),       month = t_post,       hba1c = pmax(5, v_a),       medication = "DrugA",       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ),     data.frame(       subject_id = sprintf("P%02d", i),       month = t_post,       hba1c = pmax(5, v_b),       medication = "DrugB",       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   ) }  trial_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_patients), make_patient))

title: Visualizing Longitudinal Trajectories with geom_kodom_line
text: examples use simulated HbA1c dataset: 25 patients 6–12 irregular visits 24 months. patient also fixed age covariate used later demonstrate independent aesthetic mappings.
code: set.seed(42) n_subjects <- 25 n_obs_per <- sample(6:12, n_subjects, replace = TRUE)  df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_subjects), function(i) {   n <- n_obs_per[i]   base <- rnorm(1, mean = 7.5, sd = 1.2)   trend <- rnorm(1, mean = -0.02, sd = 0.01)   time <- sort(runif(n, 0, 24))   value <- base + trend * time + rnorm(n, sd = 0.4)   data.frame(     subject_id = sprintf("P%03d", i),     visit_month = time,     relative_month = time - min(time),     hba1c = pmax(4, value),     arm = ifelse(i <= 12, "Treatment", "Control"),     age = sample(30:75, 1),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }))

title: Heatmap, Circular, and Periodic Variants
text: Two datasets used. small cohort (25 patients, irregular visits) identical companion vignette serves circular examples. large cohort (100 patients) demonstrates heatmap layout outperforms individual paths.
code: set.seed(42)  make_cohort <- function(n_subjects, seed = 42) {   set.seed(seed)   n_obs_per <- sample(6:12, n_subjects, replace = TRUE)   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_subjects), function(i) {     n <- n_obs_per[i]     base <- rnorm(1, mean = 7.5, sd = 1.2)     trend <- rnorm(1, mean = -0.02, sd = 0.01)     time <- sort(runif(n, 0, 24))     value <- base + trend * time + rnorm(n, sd = 0.4)     data.frame(       subject_id = sprintf("P%03d", i),       visit_month = time,       hba1c = pmax(4, value),       arm = ifelse(i <= round(n_subjects / 2), "Treatment", "Control"),       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   })) }  df_small <- make_cohort(25) df_large <- make_cohort(100)

text: geom_kodom_periodic() built cyclical longitudinal data — measurements repeat known period (months year, hours day, seasonal study cycles). subject occupies concentric ring; time maps angle one full revolution equals one period. avoid cycles overlapping exactly, radius expands slowly time progresses, creating star-trail spiral effect. Key difference geom_kodom_circular(): Circular: angle = subject identity; time increases outward along spoke. Periodic: angle = time within cycle; radius increases slowly separate successive cycles subject.
